intro_html:
The GRID Amendment Act has had a public hearing but no committee vote, and it lapses if it has not passed when Council Period 26 ends in January 2027; even an act the Council passes must then clear congressional review. Until then Pepco’s interconnection process applies. In the District an inverter-based system of 20 kW or less is a Level 1 application with no fee, but every application also needs a net energy metering contract, and the process runs through a city electrical inspection and a net-capable meter. Pepco puts the whole thing at about 80 business days.

Condo and co-op owners in the District already have a statutory solar right. D.C. Code §8-1774.51 bars homeowners, condominium and cooperative associations from prohibiting a “solar energy collection device”, which expressly includes “solar photovoltaic apparatus”, on an owner’s “property or residential unit”, and limits them to non-aesthetic guidelines aimed at preventing nuisance. But an association may still prohibit devices on the “common elements”, so whether a balcony panel is protected turns on whether the condominium declaration makes the balcony part of the unit or a common element. Renters get no comparable right.

faq: Can a DC condo association ban solar panels?

Not on the owner’s own property or unit. D.C. Code §8-1774.51 bars homeowners, condominium and cooperative associations from prohibiting a solar energy collection device there, and allows only non-aesthetic guidelines to prevent nuisance. Associations may still prohibit devices on common elements other than a roof covering a single unit, so how the condominium declaration classifies a balcony decides the question. This is not legal advice.
How long does Pepco take to connect a small solar system in DC?

Pepco puts its full interconnection process in the District at about 80 business days: an application with a net energy metering contract, installation, a city electrical inspection and a net-capable meter. A Level 1 application, for inverter-based systems of 20 kW or less, carries no application fee in DC.
